note:
SECOND REQUEST, same session: Malcolm also asked for the bottle text on skingenetix-hero-model-copper-peptide-2026 to be sharper and clearer. Checked at 100% per rule 3 and it is not merely soft, it is WRONG, and it is live on the homepage right now. Reading down the label in the shipped frame: 'Skingenetix' correct and sharp; 'COPPER PEPTIDE' legible but with a doubled P and a broken D; 'ADVANCED REPAIR SERUM' breaking up and very low in contrast, pale blue on blue; 'PREMIUM FORMULA' dissolved into mush; '2% GHK-CU | 30ML' pure gibberish, reading roughly '0M-0J | 5IM'.

THE CAUSE IS MEASURABLE, NOT STYLISTIC. The label is about 360px wide inside a 3072px frame, so the smallest line carries roughly 12px of cap height. No engine on the roster sets 12px type correctly — this is the MATRIXYL lesson again in a different disguise. Telling the engine to be 'sharp' cannot fix a pixel budget, so the fix is geometric: the bottle comes closer to camera. HERO3-BIGBOTTLE states the label size as a measured fraction of frame height rather than describing it, which is the only instruction that has ever survived six engines. The two other hero slots keep the shipped composition and add the sharpness and contrast demand, so Malcolm can see whether composition or pixel budget was the binding constraint.

ORIGINAL REQUEST: two live homepage images are to be re-made with the model NOT wearing a sweater and NO clothing in view at all — skingenetix-concern-firming-skin-density-2026 (index skin_concerns block c2) and skingenetix-hero-model-copper-peptide-2026 (index hero slide 3). Both currently show the same charcoal knit high neck, which came from the briefs themselves: the CONCERN-2 brief said 'wearing a high necked charcoal knit top' and HERO-D said 'a simple high necked charcoal knit top'. So this is not a generation fault to negate around — the garment was asked for, and the fix is to ask for the opposite and negate the garment as well.

SAME IMAGE, NOT A NEW ONE. He asked for the same image without the sweater, so each subject runs on TWO routes and both go in front of him:
  * _edit — the already-chosen frame goes in as the reference and the only instruction is to take the garment out and continue the bare skin. Highest chance of holding the same face, light and ground.
  * _t2i — the original brief re-written bare, reference-free. Insurance, because an edit pass tends to smooth skin texture, and skin texture is the whole point of this brand's register.
Judge them side by side; the edit route is expected to win on likeness and the t2i route on skin.

WHERE THE FRAME NOW ENDS. 'No clothes in view' means the crop has to stop before any garment could appear, so both briefs now state a positive termination — the concern tile fades the bare shoulder into the background at the bottom edge, the hero lets the shoulder run off the lower edge of the frame. Stating where skin ends is what stops an engine putting a strap or a neckline there to solve the boundary for itself. Bare shoulders and collarbone only: this is the standard beauty-editorial crop, nothing below the collarbone is in frame.

SUPPLIER NOTES. FLUX.2 is barred from reference shots, so it runs on the t2i slots only, and never on HERO3 at all because the label is legible there. Luma is reference-blind in generate-multi.py — it will return a t2i interpretation on the _edit slots too; read those as bonus alternatives, not as edits. Rule 1 still applies: every slot goes to every supplier that can take it.
